concepts.description: REST requests support GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, and OPTIONS.
GraphQL supports queries and mutations with variables, but not subscriptions.
WebSocket support is limited to basic connection and message testing.
Protocol-buffer-based gRPC service testing remains beta.
Authentication covers header API keys, bearer or JWT tokens, OAuth2 client credentials and authorization code, and Basic username/password.
Requests accept JSON, XML, form-data, and raw bodies; responses support JSON Schema and custom validation.
Development, staging, and production environments retain separate base URLs and placeholder credentials.
Related requests can be stored in reusable collections and executed with assertions.
A request may consume output produced by an earlier request.
Load testing exposes request and concurrency controls, and collections can generate Markdown API documentation.
The canonical GET example carries Accept and API-key headers; the POST example carries JSON content type plus name and email.
Validation can constrain status, headers, required object fields, and property types.
Assertions cover status, body content, headers, elapsed time, and array or string length.
Timing output distinguishes total, DNS, TCP, TLS, time-to-first-byte, download, and response-size measurements.
The mock example exposes GET and POST user routes, fixed success statuses, a fixed sample user, and a generated UUID.
Connection, timeout, authentication, and SSL or TLS failures receive clear diagnostic feedback.
Certificate validation may be skipped only in testing.
Sensitive API values belong in environment variables rather than source or test collections.
Test collections remain under version control.
Tests cover failures and edge cases in addition to happy paths.
Tests use clear names, document expected behavior, and apply response-time assertions to detect regressions.
OAuth2 authorization-code flow requires manual browser interaction.
Each uploaded test file is limited to 10MB.
Request examples, schema-validation guidance, and CI/CD integration remain linked to their respective guide paths.
